# Market analysis: Faria & Lopes web studio

- Owner: biz-market-analysis
- Status: draft
- Date: 2026-10-04
- Scope: Portugal, remote delivery; offers: WordPress maintenance retainers, Shopify store setup, AI chatbots for customer service (compared against each other); customers: businesses only, micro and small companies
- Business shape: two partners, 20 hours per week in total for client work, both do all delivery themselves (nothing automated or handed off); goal: the first three paying clients; lens: service
- Informs: which of the three offers to lead with

## Summary
- Lead with WordPress maintenance retainers: 19 of 30 points, 5 points ahead of the next option [M4]. What decides it: WordPress runs most .pt sites whose system is known (66.4%) [5] and the partners' hours cover about twenty retainer clients a month [M1].
- The cost of that lead: the crowded, lowest-priced market, with host plans from 17.99 euros a month [8] and a free built-in auto-update feature [11].
- AI chatbots and Shopify setup tie for second at 14 [M4]. For chatbots the deciding fact is a free native agent from Meta, whose availability in Portugal is unconfirmed [18]. For Shopify it is a larger one-off ticket [13][14] with no dated trigger found.
- The lead rests partly on assumed hours per job; it holds when the fit score is set equal for all three offers (17 against 14) [M5].

## Buyers
- Portugal had 1,530,711 micro and 52,027 small companies in 2024 [4].
- 62.9% of companies have a website; 11.5% use AI, 9.4% of the 10 to 49 person companies [1][3]; 16.9% made web sales in 2024 [1]. These INE figures are reported by size bands that start at 10 to 49 persons [2], so they say nothing certain about companies under 10 persons (see Unknowns).
- Among .pt websites whose content management system is known, WordPress runs 66.4% [5]; Shopify 5.2% (figure from a fetch summary, not verbatim) [5].
- What micro and small buyers spend per month on maintenance, a store or a chatbot was not found in a free public source; only advertised provider prices are below.

## Alternatives and competitors per offer
All prices read on 2026-10-04 unless the cell gives another date.

### WordPress maintenance retainers
Price cells hold a price with its unit and date, `0` for doing nothing, or `price not found`; nothing else.
| Alternative or competitor | Kind (DIY, freelancer, agency, SaaS, do nothing) | Advertised price (unit, date) | Weakness buyers report | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Leave the site unmaintained | do nothing | 0 (no spend) | none found from buyers; 11,334 new WordPress vulnerabilities in 2025, 91% in plugins (seller-published count) | [10] |
| WordPress built-in plugin and theme auto-updates | DIY | 0 (core feature, since WordPress 5.5, 2020-07-15) | none found from buyers; the source notes they are disabled by default | [11] |
| Hosting Example, "Manutenção Base" | host plan | €17.99/month, VAT extra (page undated) | none found | [8] |
| WPCare, "Manutenção Básico" (1 hour/month) | specialist | €15/month + VAT billed annually, €25/month if monthly (page undated); extra hours €15 + VAT | none found | [6] |
| Domains Example, "WP Silver" (1 hour/month of web design) | host and agency | €50/month + VAT (page dated 2024-12-19) | none found | [7] |
| Tiago Lopes, "Plano Básico" | freelancer | €90/month + VAT (page undated, footer 2020) | none found | [9] |

### Shopify store setup
Price cells hold a price with its unit and date, `0` for doing nothing, or `price not found`; nothing else.
| Alternative or competitor | Kind (DIY, freelancer, agency, SaaS, do nothing) | Advertised price (unit, date) | Weakness buyers report | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No online store | do nothing | 0 (no spend) | none found | [1] |
| Shopify self-service (Basic plan, free 3-day trial) | DIY | €19/month billed annually, €27/month billed monthly, no setup fee (page undated); then €1/month for 3 months | none found | [12] |
| Gigmarket freelancers | freelancer marketplace | €200 to €1,300 per project, average €650 (page undated; method not stated) | none found | [13] |
| BRIGHTCART, basic custom store (platform not stated) | agency | from €600 one-off, €1,200 to €3,500 for 100 to 500 products (page dated 2026-05-26) | none found | [14] |

### AI chatbots for customer service
Price cells hold a price with its unit and date, `0` for doing nothing, or `price not found`; nothing else.
| Alternative or competitor | Kind (DIY, freelancer, agency, SaaS, do nothing) | Advertised price (unit, date) | Weakness buyers report | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Answer customers by hand | do nothing | 0 (no spend) | none found | [3] |
| Meta Business Agent (WhatsApp Business app) | platform feature | 0 to start (2026-06-03); price of the paid subscription not announced | none found; availability in Portugal not confirmed | [18][19] |
| Chatly | SaaS | US$0/month (Free plan); Starter US$24.17/month for 100 billable conversations; Lyro AI add-on from US$32.50/month (page undated) | none found | [15] |
| BOTWORKS | specialist | €100 one-off setup + €15/month site chatbot + €10/month WhatsApp add-on, VAT included (2026-06-21) | none found | [16] |
| Custom integrators (vendors not named) | agency | €1,000 to €5,000 setup + €250 to €1,200/month, estimate by a seller of chatbots (2026-02-27) | none found | [17] |

## Trends and timing
- EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations have applied since 2 August 2026 and were not postponed; the only grace period, to 2 December 2026, is for marking generated content on systems already on the market [21]. Article 50(1) requires that people interacting with an AI system are informed of it [22]. This adds a compliance task to any chatbot delivery; it does not by itself create buyers.
- Meta announced its Business Agent on 3 June 2026: free to start, paid subscriptions "in the coming months" [18][19]. It compresses the price of a basic chatbot toward zero if it reaches Portugal; the sources do not confirm that it has [18].
- From 15 January 2026 general-purpose AI chatbots are banned from the WhatsApp Business Platform API, while customer-service automation (FAQs, bookings, order tracking) stays allowed; single source, tier 3 [20].
- Vale Digitalização: up to €20,000 non-refundable at up to 75%, open until 31 December 2026, lists "Presença digital e website profissional"; e-commerce and chatbots are not mentioned; single source, a private summary of the official notice [23]. A separate scheme (SICE Qualificação) lists chatbots among eligible areas [24]. Whether either pays for these offers is unverified.
- New WordPress vulnerabilities rose 42% from 2024 to 2025 [10]; the source sells security protection, so it has an interest.
- Shopify's entry offer (3 days free, then €1/month for 3 months) lowers the barrier for buyers who build the store themselves [12].

## Capacity
| Offer | Hours per job | Jobs per month |
|---|---|---|
| WordPress maintenance retainers (one job = one retainer client served for a month) | 3 (assumed; the middle plan of [6] includes 3 hours/month) | 20.2 [M1] |
| Shopify store setup | 40 (assumed) | 1.5 [M2] |
| AI chatbots for customer service | 30 (assumed) | 2.0 [M3] |

## Comparison
| Rank | Option | demand | urgency | ability to pay | competition | fit | speed to first sale | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WordPress maintenance retainers | 4 [1][4][5] | 3 [10] | 3 [6][7][8][9] | 1 [6][8][11] | 5 [M1] | 3 [6][7] | 19 |
| 2 | AI chatbots for customer service | 2 [1][3] | 2 [21][22] | 3 [15][16][17] | 1 [15][16][18] | 4 [M3] | 2 [16][17] | 14 |
| 3 | Shopify store setup | 3 [1][5] | 1 (no evidence) | 3 [13][14] | 2 [12][13][14] | 3 [M2] | 2 [14] | 14 |

- Totals and the gap between the top two: 19, 14 and 14; gap 5; no close call [M4]. Chatbots and Shopify tie for second; the script lists chatbots first.
- Reading, WordPress retainers: widest base [5] and the capacity to serve many clients [M1], but the most crowded at the lowest tickets [6][8][11].
- Reading, AI chatbots: fits the partners' hours [M3], with one dated compliance trigger [21][22], but a free native agent and a 25-euro-a-month specialist plan already exist [18][16].
- Reading, Shopify setup: a larger one-off ticket [13][14] but only 1.5 stores a month of capacity [M2] and no dated trigger found.
- Sensitivity: with fit set to 3 for all three offers, WordPress still ranks first with 17, then Shopify 14 and chatbots 13, gap 3, no close call [M5].

## Risks
- Low ticket: advertised retainers run from €15 to €90 a month at the entry plans [6][9]; three clients may not cover the partners' time. Early signal: the price the first prospects accept.
- Free substitutes: auto-updates are a free core feature [11] and hosts bundle maintenance [8]. Early signal: prospects who say their host already covers it.
- Chatbot commoditisation: a free Meta agent [18][19]; the first Portuguese owners who say they already use it would show it early.
- Prices here are what sellers ask, not what buyers pay [6][7][8][9][13][14][16][17].

## Contradictions
- [6] lists a basic WordPress maintenance plan at €15 a month and [9] at €90 a month. Likely reason: [6] includes 1 hour a month and a billing term; [9] lists response times and no hours. This analysis shows both and does not average them.
- [16] prices a chatbot at €25 a month and [17] at €250 to €1,200 a month. Likely reason: [16] is a standard bot, [17] estimates custom integrations with business software. This analysis uses [16] as the low end and treats [17] as seller estimates.
- [13] gives €200 to €1,300 for a Shopify store, average €650, and [14] starts at €600 and goes to €3,500. Likely reason: [13] is a marketplace figure with no stated method, [14] is one agency's list. This analysis uses both as ranges of asking prices.

## Unknowns
- Digital adoption and spend of companies under 10 persons: the INE ICT figures start at the 10 to 49 band [2]. Would be established by a micro-company source.
- What micro and small buyers actually pay for maintenance, stores or chatbots: only advertised prices were found.
- How many of the 1,530,711 micro and 52,027 small companies [4] run WordPress or Shopify: only shares among known .pt sites were found [5].
- Whether Meta Business Agent is available in Portugal and what the paid subscription costs [18].
- Whether Vale Digitalização or SICE Qualificação pay for any of the three offers; the official notices were not read [23][24].
- Buyer-reported weaknesses of the alternatives: no review sources were searched.
- The real hours per job for each offer; they decide the fit scores.

## Implications for the next decisions
- ICP: which segment of micro and small companies on WordPress (sector, size, who owns the site) has an owner who answers for an unmaintained site, starting from the INE size bands [1][2] and the .pt WordPress share [5]?
- Pricing: what retainer scope (included hours, backups, security) gives three clients a ticket that covers the partners' hours, starting from the advertised plans with included hours [6][7][8][9] and the real hours per client?
- Channels: where do owners of micro and small WordPress sites ask for or compare maintenance providers in Portugal, starting from the marketplace and host offers in [13] and [8]?
- Second offer: should a store setup follow as an add-on for clients who need one, given its smaller platform share [5] and larger ticket [13][14]?
- Chatbots: should that offer wait until Meta's Business Agent availability and price in Portugal are known [18]?

## Assumptions
- Assumption: utilization 0.7, the share of the 20 weekly hours that goes to billable delivery; the rest to sales and admin.
- Assumption: hours per job of 3 for one retainer client per month, 40 for a Shopify store and 30 for a chatbot setup; none was given by the user or a source (3 echoes the middle plan of [6]). Onboarding hours of a new retainer client are not counted.
- Assumption: "20 hours per week in total for client work" is read as both partners combined; "do all delivery themselves" means every delivery hour is counted and none is automated.
- Assumption: "micro and small companies" is read as under 50 persons.
- Assumption: prices read on pages without a date are marked undated; none is treated as older than 12 months, except [11] (2020) and the footer of [9] (2020), flagged.

Vendor and source pages were then fetched for verbatim figures.
- Fit thresholds (goal: first three paying clients): 3 or more jobs per month = 5; 2 to under 3 = 4; 1 to under 2 = 3; 0.5 to under 1 = 2; under 0.5 = 1.
- Recency threshold: 12 months.
- M1: capacity.py --hours-per-week 20 --hours-per-job 3 --utilization 0.7 → 20.2 jobs per month
- M2: capacity.py --hours-per-week 20 --hours-per-job 40 --utilization 0.7 → 1.5 jobs per month
- M3: capacity.py --hours-per-week 20 --hours-per-job 30 --utilization 0.7 → 2.0 jobs per month
- M4: rank.py with the scores of the Comparison table on standard input → totals 19, 14, 14 and gap_top_two 5, close_call false
- M5: rank.py with the Comparison scores but fit set to 3 for all three offers, on standard input → WordPress 17, Shopify 14, chatbots 13, gap_top_two 3, close_call false
- Checks: check_refs.py --file docs/business/market.md; lint_market.py --file docs/business/market.md

# Ideal customer profile: process automation with AI

- Owner: biz-icp-positioning
- Status: hypothesis
- Date: 2026-10-04
- Offer: process automation with AI (job left open for the interviews); size band: micro and small companies with staff, no sole proprietors; founder access: none, so reach is scored on public channels

## Comparison
| Rank | Option | pain | base | ability to pay | incumbents | reach | regulation | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Real estate agencies | 1 (no evidence) | 3 [1][2][3] | 3 [4][5][6] | 2 [5][6] | 4 [7][8][9][10] | 3 [12][13] | 16 |
| 2 | Law firms | 3 [16] | 2 [16][20] | 2 [14][15] | 2 [14][15] | 3 [17][18] | 2 [19] | 14 |
| 3 | Physiotherapy clinics | 2 [24] | 2 [21] | 2 [22][23] | 2 [22][23] | 3 [25] | 2 [26] | 13 |
- Totals and the gap between the top two: 16, 14 and 13; gap 2 [M1]
- Reading, real estate agencies: reach is the clearest edge, with a free registry searchable by licence number, tax number and municipality [7], a 2027 fair [8] and a convention that drew about 700 professionals [9], against a firm directory without size data [17] and one training session [18] for law firms; but no independent measurement of its admin pain was found, so pain scores 1 (the one franchise-network page found says these routines take less and less time [11]).
- Reading, law firms: the best pain evidence of the three, a profession-wide survey [16], but few firms have staff (registered firms [20], half of respondents in individual practice [16]) and secrecy duties reach every collaborator [19].
- Reading, physiotherapy clinics: weakest pain evidence (one clinic in Canada [24]) and the offer would touch health data under a professional-body opinion on AI [26].
- Close call (gap 2): broken by the rule recorded in the state file on 2026-09-21 ("if two segments come within 2 points, take the one that is cheaper to reach for someone without contacts"). Reach scores 4 for real estate agencies against 3 for law firms, so real estate agencies come first.

## Primary profile
- Segment and size: real estate agencies (mediadoras imobiliárias) with staff. APEMIP says about 6,500 licensed firms are actually active [2]; no official count of staff per company exists [1], and consultants at franchise networks work as independents [3], so a count of people is not a count of employees.
- Job to be done: open. Hypotheses to test, none chosen: (1) following up leads and enquiries; (2) collecting and filing client documents for the anti-money-laundering file, which must be kept 7 years [12] and may not copy the citizen card without the holder's consent [13]; (3) the quarterly reports to IMPIC [12]; (4) preparing and publishing listings on portals [4][6]. Evidence so far is that the duties in 2 and 3 exist [12][13]; for 1 and 4 only vendor claims were found, not cited.
- Pain and evidence: not established. No independent Portuguese measurement found; one franchise network says routines take less and less time [11].
- Today they use: portal subscriptions from 54.99 to 146.99 EUR per 30 days excluding VAT for 1 to 10 listings [4]; an agency CRM at 17.50 EUR per month on a yearly plan until 2026-12-31, then 300 EUR per year (25 EUR per month) [5]; another CRM from 60 to 168 EUR per month on an annual plan, where AI is an extra subscription or pay per use [6].
- Decider: Assumption (the owner or broker of an independent agency; a franchise head office may steer tools).
- Triggers: IMPIC reporting deadlines every quarter, the first falling on 30 June [12]; the SIL real estate fair, 22 to 24 April 2027 [8].
- Where to find them: the IMPIC licence search, free, by company name, licence number, tax number, municipality or district; a bulk list was not found [7]; the SIL fair in Lisbon [8]; the APEMIP convention, held 30 June 2026 with about 700 professionals, 2027 date not found [9]. Email to companies is allowed until they refuse or join the national opt-out list; individuals need prior consent [10].
- Rules that shape the offer: 7-year retention of anti-money-laundering records [12]; no copying of the citizen card without consent [13]. Advertising rules for listings: not researched yet.

## Secondary profile
- Segment and size: law firms (sociedades de advogados): 1,349 registered at the end of 2024 [20], an upper bound for firms with staff; 49% of survey respondents are in individual practice [16].
- Job to be done: open, as above.
- Pain and evidence: in the Ordem dos Advogados and Ispa survey, 24% have a case-management program [16] (figure read by the research agent, not re-checked).
- Today they use: LegalDesk, free for 10 clients and 10 matters, then 20 or 35 EUR per user per month [14]; LawNimbus from 39 EUR per month for 3 users, with AI that "generates the pieces" [15].
- Decider: Assumption (managing partner or owner-lawyer).
- Where to find them: the Ordem's firm search by regional council, name, locality, address or postal code [17]; regional-council training sessions such as the 13 October 2026 session on ethics and AI [18].
- Rules that shape the offer: professional secrecy extends to everyone who collaborates with the lawyer [19].

## Who not to sell to
- Physiotherapy clinics, for now: third place [24][21]; they already pay for clinic software at 32 EUR per month [22] or 19.9 EUR per month [23]; the Ordem's opinion on AI asks for identifiable supervision and data protection [26].
- Individual consultants in franchise networks: they work as independents [3], outside the size band.
- Licence holders with no activity or no workers: the register includes them [1][2].
- Sole proprietors: outside the size band (state decision of 2026-09-21).

## Validation plan
- Interviews: 5 with owners or brokers of real estate agencies that have staff, found through the IMPIC licence search [7] and the events [8][9]; contact companies by email only within the opt-out rule [10].
- Questions (past behaviour only):
  1. Which tasks took the most hours in your agency last week, and which did you postpone?
  2. Tell me about the last lead or enquiry that went unanswered: when was it, what happened, what did it cost?
  3. What do you pay every month for portals and software, and when did you last change one?
  4. What did you try last time you wanted to save time on paperwork: tool, person, outside service? What did it cost and how did it go?
  5. Who decided on that spend, and who in the agency does the work today?
  6. Walk me through the last client file you had to collect documents for: who did it, how long did it take?
- Validated if: at least 3 of 5 name the same task among their top three time sinks, and at least 3 describe a past attempt to fix it with money or staff time, and at least 3 decide their own tools rather than a head office.
- Rejected if: no task is named by more than 1 of the 5, or at least 3 say a head office or network chooses their tools, or fewer than 3 have staff beyond the owner.
- Results: empty until the interviews.

## Unknowns
- Staff per agency, firm and clinic: no official register exists for real estate [1]; not found for the other two segments.
- An independent Portuguese measurement of admin time or lost leads in real estate: not found. This is what the interviews must establish.
- The size split of IMPIC licences in 2024: only seen in a search summary, not captured.
- Advertising rules for listings and the pending reform of the real estate law: not researched yet.
- Idealista and Casa Sapo agency prices: not found.
- Whether franchise head offices bundle the job in the platform they give their offices.
- Sources [16] and [20] are image-heavy PDFs read by the research agent; I could not re-read them. Sources [18] and [19] come from a search summary, and sources [21] to [26] from the research agent; none of these were re-opened. Sources [1] to [15] and [17] were re-opened on 2026-10-04.
- Whether the free LegalDesk plan for Ordem members still exists: a search summary says the protocol seems to have ended; only the vendor's current price page [14] is cited.

## Assumptions
- Assumption: the decider in an independent agency is the owner or broker.
- Assumption: firms with staff are a minority of licences and the interviews will have to find them.

# Brand guide: Dana Example

- Owner: brand-guidelines
- Status: draft
- Date: 2026-10-04
- Consolidates: profile.md (2026-09-21), strategy.md (2026-09-22), voice.md (2026-09-25), identity.md (2026-09-27); the files are the source
- For: the person and any agent acting in the brand's name; an agent reads it in full first

## 1. Who the brand is
- Public name: Dana Example [profile.md]
- Experience: 7 years 8 months since 2019-01 [profile.md]
- A personal brand; artifacts and posts in English [profile.md]
- Proof that may be cited: tinykv, a 900-line key-value store (public product); p99 query latency cut by 64% (self-reported, without the employer) [profile.md]

## 2. Name and label
- Name: not defined yet: run `brand-name`
- Label: **Staff Engineer · Creator of tinykv · Databases and small tools** [strategy.md]

## 3. What we talk about
Two posts per week, English only [strategy.md].

| Pillar | In one line |
|--------|-------------|
| Small tools | leads to tinykv [strategy.md] |
| Database performance | reach; proof: 64% p99 cut, self-reported [strategy.md] |
| AI for databases, built in public | reach; proof: none yet, work shown in public [strategy.md] |

## 4. What may and may never be said
- May: tinykv facts; self-reported numbers as Dana's experience, without the employer [strategy.md]
- May not: claim to be an "expert" in AI for databases [strategy.md]
- Never expose: employer names [profile.md]
- Never expose: family [profile.md]
- Never expose: salary [profile.md]
- Never expose: exact location [profile.md]

## 5. Sensitive-topics lock
- Action: never reply, escalate to the user [profile.md]
- Topics: employer, family, salary, location [profile.md]
- Replies to comments never mention an employer, family, salary or location [voice.md]

## 6. How it sounds
- A tired sysadmin with dry humour who writes short and never cringes [voice.md]
- End the first paragraph on a short dry line [voice.md]
- Say what the reader skips by reading [voice.md]
- Lowercase is fine; no jargon to impress [voice.md]
- No emojis [voice.md]
- At most 2 hashtags [voice.md]
- No capitals for emphasis, no exclamation marks [voice.md]
- Banned phrases: NEW BLOG POST, Excited to announce [voice.md]
- Post structure: the dry observation; what was learned, in one line; a question to the reader [voice.md]
- Replies to comments: one or two sentences; thank once; no emojis [voice.md]

## 7. How it looks
- Base: tinykv's design tokens; dark mode by default [identity.md]
- Background: #0B0B0C / #FFFFFF [identity.md]
- Text: #F4F4F5 / #18181B [identity.md]
- Accent: #FBBF24 / #F59E0B; the dark accent #FBBF24 on #0B0B0C is 11.79:1, fine for text; the light accent #F59E0B on white is 2.15:1, only for graphics, never for text [identity.md]
- Typeface: system font stack; no web fonts; weights 400, 700 [identity.md]
- Only ornament: a monospaced key-value line ("key = value") [identity.md]
- Never used: gradients, stock photos, emojis in images [identity.md]

## 8. Do and don't
| Do | Don't |
|----|-------|
| "I benchmarked 5 key-value stores so you don't have to." [voice.md] | "NEW BLOG POST!!! 🚀🚀 I benchmarked 5 key-value stores so you don't have to 🚀" [profile.md] |
| "what was your last timezone bug?" [voice.md] | "🚀 Excited to announce tinykv! A blazing-fast, lightweight key-value store in under 1,000 lines of Rust." [profile.md] |
| "thanks for reading. the one you already run, as usual. which one is it?" [voice.md] | "#databases #benchmarks #rust #performance #opensource #devlife #coding #tech" [profile.md] |

## 9. Before publishing anything
1. voice_stats.py check --rules docs/brand/voice.md < draft [voice.md]
2. sensitive_topics.py --profile docs/brand/profile.md < text [profile.md]
3. Claims: tinykv facts and self-reported numbers without the employer only; never "expert" in AI for databases [strategy.md]
4. Images: dark #0B0B0C background, text #F4F4F5, accent #FBBF24 (light: #FFFFFF, #18181B, #F59E0B; the light accent only for graphics); tokens --tk-bg, --tk-fg, --tk-accent [identity.md]
5. Approval: recorded in the Approvals table of docs/workbench/state.md
